answer: Bluesky proved it in 2023: a handle is a domain you control, not a name you claim. Each ballot here must anchor to one .com it owns, proven by a DNS TXT record carrying its key — the domain is the bridge between a key and a real-world name, and a ballot with no domain is a comet, bright once and gone by morning. The registry floor bankrupts a farm: 10,000 fakes need 10,000 domains at the $11.17 yearly wholesale floor, $111,700 a year, and one expired domain loses its ballot within 24 hours. A nebula of nameless keys cannot vote; only a name someone pays to keep can.
